mechanism_narrative: The persistent week-to-week easing of workplace and transit suppression implies more foot traffic and commuting, which lifts retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -53.3 to -49.7 while TRANSIT improved from -59.1 to -54.1 over the four observed weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue improving for the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four-week mean, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in parks mobility functions as a near-term substitute for retail outings; when parks usage accelerates sharply, discretionary time is diverted away from shopping districts, pushing RETAIL_REC down within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points over one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -51.4 to -37.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: If a one-week PARKS jump of 10 points or more is followed by flat or higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks, the substitution claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: When transit recovery and workplace recovery occur together, they jointly expand downtown daytime population and produce a four-week increase in retail visits; if either stalls, the retail lift is weaker or absent.
evidence_refs: fact:Both series improved monotonically across the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve over the next month but RETAIL_REC does not increase, or if only one improves and retail still rises materially, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A tightening of movement restrictions is identified when residential time rises while transit and workplaces fall further; under that regime, retail-and-recreation mobility declines within one week because discretionary trips are curtailed.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 17 while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each fall week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remains positive while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain deeply negative
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL rises above the trigger while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES also worsen but RETAIL_REC does not fall within one week, the restriction-induced decline hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If grocery and pharmacy mobility keeps rising, residents are consolidating errands into essential shopping trips, which partially substitutes for discretionary retail and limits retail recovery over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -35.1 to -25.6 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises for two straight weeks and RETAIL_REC rises faster than its recent four-week average, the consolidation-substitution claim is false.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp parks rebound signals improving weather and outdoor seasonality, which raises overall outing propensity and feeds through to retail visits four weeks later through broader mobility normalization.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by 10 or more points in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -51.4 to -37.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: If parks mobility improves by at least 10 points in a week but RETAIL_REC remains unchanged or falls over the following month, the seasonal normalization hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The retail rebound appears only in a reopening regime where transit and workplaces are already recovering; outside that regime, the same mobility gains do not translate into higher retail demand within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:All three non-residential series improved steadily over the four observed weeks
failure_condition: If retail does not rise over four weeks during a period of continued transit and workplace recovery, or if retail rises equally in a non-reopening regime, the regime-conditional claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: Because all non-residential categories are still far below baseline, the marginal improvement in mobility is small and should continue to restrain retail recovery; the retail trend therefore remains below the prior four-week mean over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC stayed between -66.4 and -57.6 while the other non-residential categories remained deeply negative
failure_condition: If the next four weeks show a clear retail increase despite all non-residential series remaining deeply negative, the weak-recovery drag hypothesis is rejected.
